sections.body_markdown:
Market commentary is full of confident calls made after the fact. A stock drops, someone posts the bearish screenshot they saved. A stock rallies, someone says they saw it coming. The misses usually disappear.

We reviewed Walnut's durable production records to see what the confirmation system had actually stored before several recent moves. The audit found five qualifying examples where the stored direction matched what the stock did next. It also found one clear miss in Meta.

The purpose of this review is not to claim that Walnut can predict exact returns. It is to show how the confirmation system can identify when the available evidence is leaning bullish, bearish, or conflicted, and how that judgment changes as new information enters the model.

| Ticker | Stored signal | Start close | July 29 close | Move |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [NBIS](/ticker/NBIS) | 73/100 strong bearish | $261.15 | $148.27 | -43.22% |
| [INFQ](/ticker/INFQ) | 73/100 strong bearish | $14.21 | $8.83 | -37.86% |
| [MU](/ticker/MU) | 74/100 strong bearish | $866.29 | $739.00 | -14.69% |
| [SPCX](/ticker/SPCX) | 76/100 strong bearish | $131.11 | $112.54 | -14.16% |
| [BMNR](/ticker/BMNR) | 60/100 strong bullish | $15.44 | $16.59 | +7.45% |
| [META](/ticker/META) | 72/100 bullish miss | $645.69 | $586.49 | -9.17% |

The first five examples moved in the same direction as the stored signal. Meta moved the other way.
sections.heading: Five signals that lined up with the move that followed, plus one that did not

sections.body_markdown:
The review used durable production records from `confirmation_monitoring_events` and closing prices from `price_cache`.

| Rule | How this audit applied it |
| --- | --- |
| Minimum score | The stored score had to be at least 60. |
| Timing | The event had to occur before the measured price move. |
| Direction | The direction had to be recorded in production at the time. |
| Start price | The starting price came from the next available stored close, except when the event date itself had the qualifying close. |
| End price | The ending price came from the latest stored close on July 29, 2026. |
| Reconstruction | Old signals were not rebuilt using current data, and missing component histories were not filled in. |

The audit did not use intraday highs or lows to improve the result. For NBIS, the durable historical record proves the score, direction, band, date, and subsequent price move, but it does not preserve the full historical component payload for the June 28 score.

These examples are not a complete performance study. They are audited case studies drawn from qualifying stored events.
sections.heading: How the audit was done

sections.body_markdown:
On June 28, Walnut recorded NBIS moving from mixed to bearish. The score increased from 56 to 73, which placed the setup in the strong bearish range.

The next available closing price was $261.15 on June 29. By July 29, NBIS had closed at $148.27. The measured move was -43.22%.

| Date | Close | Source |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 2026-06-29 | $261.15 | price_cache start close |
| 2026-07-29 | $148.27 | price_cache latest stored close |
| Move | -43.22% | Recalculated from closes |

The stored record proves that Walnut had a strong bearish judgment before the larger decline. It does not prove that Walnut expected a 43% drop, and it does not show that the signal stayed bearish every day afterward.

The historical component payload for the June 28 snapshot was not preserved, so we cannot accurately recreate the exact mix of inputs behind that score. The score, direction, date, and subsequent price move are all supported by the production record.

NBIS is still useful as a case study because the warning appeared while the stock was trading above $260, before the decline was complete.
sections.heading: NBIS: Strong bearish confirmation before a 43% decline

sections.body_markdown:
On June 19, Walnut recorded INFQ moving from mixed to bearish. The score rose from 59 to 73.

The next available close was $14.21 on June 22. By July 29, the stock had fallen to $8.83. The measured move was -37.86%.

| Date | Close | Source |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 2026-06-22 | $14.21 | price_cache start close |
| 2026-07-29 | $8.83 | price_cache latest stored close |
| Move | -37.86% | Recalculated from closes |

This example shows how a material change in confirmation can appear before a much larger price adjustment. The system had already moved to a strong bearish judgment while the stock was still trading above $14.
sections.heading: INFQ: Bearish confirmation before a 38% decline

sections.body_markdown:
Micron's qualifying signal came later in the period. On July 20, Walnut recorded MU moving from mixed to bearish. The score increased from 59 to 74.

MU closed at $866.29 on July 20. By July 29, it had fallen to $739.00. The measured move was -14.69%.

| Date | Close | Source |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 2026-07-20 | $866.29 | price_cache start close |
| 2026-07-29 | $739.00 | price_cache latest stored close |
| Move | -14.69% | Recalculated from closes |

This signal should only be discussed from July 20 onward. The stored production record does not support saying that Walnut held the same bearish view in late June.

The Micron example also shows why a low or falling valuation multiple cannot be read in isolation. In cyclical sectors, earnings, margins, pricing, and market expectations can change quickly. Walnut's confirmation system is intended to show when the broader setup is weakening even when part of the valuation story still appears attractive.
sections.heading: MU: Bearish confirmation before a 15% decline

sections.body_markdown:
On July 15, Walnut recorded SPCX at 76/100 strong bearish after the setup upgraded from weaker bearish confirmation.

The next available closing price was $131.11 on July 16. By July 29, SPCX had closed at $112.54. The measured move was -14.16%.

| Date | Close | Source |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 2026-07-16 | $131.11 | price_cache start close |
| 2026-07-29 | $112.54 | price_cache latest stored close |
| Move | -14.16% | Recalculated from closes |

The stored event shows that bearish confirmation strengthened before the measured decline. The case study does not rely on reconstructed component data or a retrospective explanation of what the model should have seen.
sections.heading: SPCX: Stronger bearish confirmation before another leg lower

sections.body_markdown:
On July 16, Walnut recorded BMNR moving from mixed to bullish. The score increased from 56 to 60.

BMNR closed at $15.44 that day. By July 29, it had reached $16.59. The measured move was +7.45%.

| Date | Close | Source |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 2026-07-16 | $15.44 | price_cache start close |
| 2026-07-29 | $16.59 | price_cache latest stored close |
| Move | +7.45% | Recalculated from closes |

This was a smaller move than the bearish examples, but it shows that Walnut's system can also turn constructive when the evidence improves.

The 7.45% gain was not forecast in advance. It was the observed return after the bullish event was stored.
sections.heading: BMNR: Bullish confirmation before a 7% gain

sections.body_markdown:
On July 20, Walnut recorded Meta moving from mixed to bullish. The score increased from 59 to 72.

Meta closed at $645.69 on July 20. By July 29, it had fallen to $586.49. The measured move was -9.17%.

| Date | Close | Source |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 2026-07-20 | $645.69 | price_cache start close |
| 2026-07-29 | $586.49 | price_cache latest stored close |
| Move | -9.17% | Recalculated from closes |

This was a miss.

A confirmation score reflects the evidence available at the time. It does not remove market risk, and it does not guarantee that price will move in the same direction. New information can change the setup quickly, and even a strong score can be wrong.

Meta is included because any serious review of Walnut's historical signals should include both successful and unsuccessful examples.
sections.heading: META: A bullish signal followed by a decline

sections.body_markdown:
The audit shows that Walnut's stored judgments sometimes appeared before meaningful moves in the same direction.

| Observed pattern | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Four strong bearish setups preceded material declines. | Walnut can surface risk when multiple sources weaken. |
| One bullish setup preceded a gain. | The system can turn constructive when the evidence improves. |
| One bullish signal failed. | Confirmation is useful, but it is not certainty. |
| Judgments updated as new evidence entered the model. | Users should monitor changes instead of treating any one score as permanent. |

For investors, the practical use is not a promise of certainty. It is having a documented view of whether the evidence is improving, weakening, or conflicted before making a decision.

| Investor use | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Recognize when a popular story is losing support. | A stock narrative can stay confident after the data starts weakening. |
| See when several sources of evidence point the same way. | Agreement across sources can make a setup easier to evaluate. |
| Notice when fundamentals and price action disagree. | Conflicts can flag situations that deserve more caution. |
| Monitor when a prior thesis has materially changed. | A useful signal is one that can update. |
| Compare setups across stocks using a consistent framework. | Consistency makes decisions easier to review later. |
sections.heading: What these examples suggest

sections.body_markdown:
This review is not a full performance study.

| Limitation | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| It does not establish Walnut's overall hit rate across every ticker or signal. | A complete backtest would need a larger fixed sample. |
| It does not prove a user would have entered or exited at the measured prices. | Case-study returns are not portfolio returns. |
| It does not establish causation. | A stored signal can align with a move without causing it. |
| It does not guarantee future results. | Historical outcomes do not remove market risk. |
| It does not prove Walnut held the same direction throughout each period. | Scores and judgments changed as new information entered the system. |

A full performance study would require a larger sample, fixed methodology, complete historical component storage, benchmark comparisons, and analysis across different market conditions.
sections.heading: What these examples do not prove

sections.body_markdown:
Historical examples are useful, but investors make decisions with current data. Walnut continuously updates its view as price action, fundamentals, insider activity, Congress activity, institutional positioning, options flow, and macro evidence change.

The current setup may look very different from the original historical signal.

| Current view | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Confirmation score | Whether evidence is bullish, bearish, mixed, or neutral now. |
| What changed | The data categories that moved the judgment. |
| Evidence | The support behind the current setup. |
| Risks | What could invalidate the thesis. |
| Watch items | What to monitor next. |

[See the current setup](/search)

sections.body_markdown:
Walnut Premium is built for investors who want a clearer view of the full setup before making a decision.

| Fundamentals | Compare price action with business and valuation context. |
| Price and volume | Track market behavior around the thesis. |

sections.heading: Premium

sections.body_markdown:
Walnut Pro adds deeper positioning data for investors who want to see more of what is happening beneath the headline.

| Pro includes | Research use |
| --- | --- |
| Institutional activity | See how larger holders are moving. |
| Options flow | Track positioning that may not appear in headline fundamentals. |
| Deeper positioning context | Compare the signal with broader market behavior. |
| Macro positioning | Understand how the setup fits the larger backdrop. |
| Market Pressure | Evaluate pressure beneath the surface. |
| Applicable Premium capabilities | Keep the deeper data connected to the full research workflow. |

The confirmation score remains separate from the underlying data categories. It is Walnut's judgment layer, not a replacement for the data supporting it.
